question: Does semantic-equivalent separation persist across independently justified resistance constructions?
pair_definition: unordered pairs within each verified semantic class

resistance_families.rationale: Preserve the already-frozen v1 structural convention so robustness is tested against the originally observed phenomenon.
resistance_families.formal_rule: Recursive canonical AST alignment; operator substitution 1; input-index substitution 1; subtree deletion 1 per node; subtree insertion 2 per node; root kind/arity change is delete-plus-insert.

resistance_families.rationale: Use a conventional unweighted edit interpretation in which each primitive structural edit has equal unit cost and direction is not privileged by asymmetric insertion/deletion pricing.
resistance_families.formal_rule: Recursive canonical AST alignment; operator substitution 1; input-index substitution 1; subtree deletion 1 per node; subtree insertion 1 per node; root kind/arity change is delete-plus-insert.

resistance_families.rationale: Treat representational edits as hierarchy-sensitive: edits at deeper AST levels carry larger local cost because they modify increasingly committed structural detail. This is a distinct weighting principle rather than a change to the v1 insertion/deletion ratio.
resistance_families.formal_rule: Recursive canonical AST alignment with operation and input-index substitution cost depth+1, and node deletion/insertion cost depth+1 for each subtree node at relative depth; root kind/arity change is weighted delete-plus-insert.

independence_rule: Families are counted as distinct robustness constructions only when their rationale and cost rule differ materially; parameter-only perturbations of one family are not additional robustness witnesses.
analysis_order: freeze all family rationales, rules, parameters, and implementation
verify and load literal certified fixtures
compute full outgoing profiles for every family
derive S_k_profile within verified semantic classes
compute pairwise intersections and Jaccard matrices
interpret only after all calculations complete
exclusions: claim that any resistance family is intrinsic or uniquely correct

interpretation.high_stability: Repeated separation of the same semantic-equivalent pairs across materially distinct resistance constructions weakens the explanation that the v1 phenomenon is specific to one arbitrary cost convention.
interpretation.low_stability: Low overlap indicates that transition structure depends materially on the chosen resistance convention; this is itself an empirical result and is not treated as assay failure.
interpretation.invariance_restored: A family with little or no separation shows that semantic invariance can be restored under that alternative construction.

claim_ceiling: The robustness assay can establish cross-convention stability or dependence of semantic-equivalent transition separation within the certified finite universe. It cannot establish intrinsic geometry, future predictive value, behavioral causality, or completeness of the representation space.
